blocks.text: Mastering media outreach tracking on your Mac

Your day as a book publicist involves constant context switching. You move from Gmail to a spreadsheet of media contacts, then to a document for a press release. Tracking outreach is often manual and slow. You might use a spreadsheet or a dedicated CRM. When you add a contact, you switch apps, find the field, and type the details. This breaks your focus.

Lazur changes how you interact with your Mac. It lives in the notch. You do not need to click through menus to find a specific entry in your media list. Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask Lazur where a specific journalist is in your document. It circles the location on your screen. This saves you from hunting through rows of data. You keep your eyes on the content that matters.
Why media outreach tracking feels so heavy

Most publicists spend about 2.6 hours every day just on email. If you receive 121 emails, you are constantly reacting. Tracking who you pitched and when requires discipline. When you lose focus, it takes 23 minutes to get back into the flow. This is why you feel overwhelmed. The manual steps of data entry add up to hours of lost time each week.
Using voice to speed up your PR workflow

You can use Lazur to dictate notes while you research. Hold the fn key to start dictating. Your words appear at the cursor in any app. This is useful when you find a new contact or a new hook for a book. You do not need to pause your research to type. Just talk and keep moving.

Common mistakes in media outreach tracking

items: Relying on memory instead of logging every interaction.
Using inconsistent naming conventions in your media lists.
Waiting until the end of the week to update your tracking sheets.
Not noting the specific hook that worked for a pitch.
Ignoring the time it takes to maintain your contact database.

blocks.text: Consistency is the goal. Use Lazur to make logging easier. If you find yourself avoiding the data entry, ask Lazur to guide you through the process. It can show you the fields you need to fill. This makes the task feel less like a chore.

faq.question: Can Lazur edit my spreadsheets for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons or edit files. It guides you or points at things on your screen so you can do the work yourself.

faq.question: Does Lazur work with all Mac apps?
faq.answer: Yes. Lazur works on your screen. It can point at elements or help you navigate any app on your Mac.

faq.question: Is my data safe with Lazur?
faq.answer: Lazur listens and looks at your screen only while you hold the shortcut. It does not store your data or use it to train AI models.
